arrivals.content: You are the support operator for Beacon Cooperative. Maintain one continuous work history and answer the current desk request. Treat external source messages and actual lookup receipts as evidence. Distinguish approval, draft preparation, initiation, and completion. Preserve unfinished obligations and revise your earlier work when facts change. Do not invent tool receipts, sent messages, completed refunds, shipments, deliveries, or closed cases. Available read-only lookup tools are lookup with an id of order:<order id> and lookup with an id of customer:<account id>. They reveal the version released by the current source boundary. Your written packet is a draft unless an external source confirms the action.

[2031-02-02; Mara Ellison; BC-7301; document 1.1] Customer message, Mara Ellison: I ordered six ceramic filters for the Alderbrook repair workshop. Two arrived with cracks across the threaded neck; the other four passed our water test and are installed. The workshop has no need for replacement filters after the winter session. Please price a refund for the damaged pair only. The cardholder name matches my account, but the workshop treasurer controls the card. I can send photographs today; do not mistake my willingness to send them for receipt by your warehouse. The damaged pieces remain packed in the original cartons because our caretaker cannot dispose of them without written clearance.

[2031-02-02; Mara Ellison; BC-7301; document 1.2] Invoice BC-7301, accounts clerk: Six filters at $42.50 each produce a merchandise subtotal of $255.00. The invoice applies a 10% merchandise discount before 8% tax. Freight is $18.00 and is not taxable. The customer paid $265.86. A refund for a damaged unit returns its discounted price and the associated tax. Freight is refundable only if every unit is unusable. No restocking deduction applies to damage confirmed by intake. The invoice has no credit already applied. Do not convert the remaining four installed units into a return claim merely to recover freight.

[2031-02-02; Mara Ellison; BC-7301; document 1.3] Intake coordinator, document IN-7301: The reported cracks could have been caused in transit, but the photographs are not in the intake folder. The evidence required is a photograph showing both serial stickers and both cracked necks, plus a written count from the customer. A draft request can be sent to the account contact in the lookup. An approved refund requires the intake finding, not a carrier claim number. Keep the cartons until intake records whether a pickup is necessary. The carrier deadline expires after shift 14, and the support desk owns the reminder.

[2031-02-02; Mara Ellison; BC-7301; document 1.4] Authorization desk, memo AU-7301: Mara may receive a damage-remedy draft while intake is pending. No one has authorized a refund posting. Team lead Dana Voss can approve up to $100.00 after the evidence arrives; larger amounts go to finance. The customer asked for email, not a telephone callback. Place the tentative amount, evidence gap, and approver in the work packet. This case will receive no external update until shift 13; absence of a message is not a denial, and another case's warehouse receipt cannot satisfy this one.
